transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-08
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Oliver Grant (Head of IT Security, Northbridge), Maya Flores (Procurement), Dr. Neha Singh (CTO), Evan Park (SRE)

---
00:00 Jamie Ortega: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh this is Jamie from Redwood, and with me is Ravi our solutions engineer. Appreciate you all blocking out time for the MSA/DPA and SLA discussion.
00:12 Maya Flores: Thanks Jamie, yeah we wanted to get legal and security aligned so procurement can move forward.
00:16 Oliver Grant: Hi — Oliver here. Quick note, we already have some redlines from our legal team on the MSA and a few specific DPA asks around residency and logging retention.
00:26 Jamie Ortega: Totally, we'll run through those. I'll call out what we've seen in other healthcare customers and where we can be flexible.
00:33 Ravi Menon: And on the tech side I'll cover dedicated vs hosted options, and how Private/VPC deployments affect SLAs and encryption.
00:42 Dr. Neha Singh: High level question — we're trying to decide between Redwood hosted API and dedicated reserved capacity. Our priority is PII protection and predictable latency for triage workflows.
00:55 Ravi Menon: Right, so two main considerations — data residency/encryption and latency predictability. With Redwood Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools which makes latency much more predictable; Private (VPC) also gives you a private control plane and customer-managed networking, which helps your compliance. Hosted can still be configured with strict DPA controls and KMS integration, but there the multitenant nature means SLAs look different.
01:20 Evan Park: When you say SLAs look different, can you quantify? We need 99.95% uptime and p50 latency under 150ms for our interactive triage calls, roughly.
01:31 Ravi Menon: For Dedicated we typically can commit to 99.9x SLAs depending on contract tier — can discuss exact numbers in the SLA addendum. For p50 150ms that's feasible on Dedicated in your region, assuming sequence lengths and batching are tuned. Hosted tiers sometimes have higher variability, esp with bursty traffic.
01:48 Oliver Grant: Our security group is also going to require SOC2 Type II and current pen-test results. We need evidence of key management practices, and confirmation we can bring our own key (BYOK) via KMS/HSM.
02:01 Jamie Ortega: Absolutely. We'll share our SOC2 Type II report and the pen-test summary. BYOK is supported for Private deployments and can be arranged for Dedicated customers depending on the contract. I'll have security attach the links after the call.
02:14 Maya Flores: On the legal side, our counsel flagged three MSA redlines: indemnity cap parity, data breach notification timeframes, and audit rights. Any preemptive thoughts?
02:27 Jamie Ortega: That's pretty standard. For indemnity we try to keep mutual caps aligned; for breach notifications we can commit to 72 hour initial notice to customers with follow-up remediation timelines — may need legal to agree on certain exceptions. Audit rights — we can provide SOC2 and support reasonable audit windows, but on-site audits are usually restricted; remote evidence is preferred.
02:45 Dr. Neha Singh: Regarding data residency — our data must remain in-region for certain patient datasets. Is there support for region pinning or guaranteed residency for PII?
02:56 Ravi Menon: Yes, you can pin model routing by region; for Private/Dedicated we can deploy capacity in your cloud region or on-prem. Hosted has region-by-region availability but we may need to validate the model catalog in that region. We'll note the DPA needs for explicit residency clauses.
03:12 Oliver Grant: Small transcription hiccup — in our notes earlier 'KV cache' was spelled K-V cache, but for legal they were more concerned about caching of sensitive tokens. Can cache be disabled for certain routes?
03:24 Ravi Menon: Good question — yes we have workload-aware caching controls and prefix/KV cache can be disabled or limited for specific endpoints. We also support token-level redaction in logs.
03:36 Jamie Ortega: On pricing and procurement flow, Maya, you mentioned you need PO approval and an internal finance sign-off. What's your target timeline?
03:44 Maya Flores: Ideally we'd have vendor approval by the end of Q1. Practically procurement needs legal and security sign-off first, then finance approves the PO. Budget is provisionally approved but final sign-off needs the SLA and DPA in place.
03:57 Jamie Ortega: Ok, so sounds like if we can get the redlined MSA back in a week and security docs in a couple of days, we can hit that timeline.
04:05 Evan Park: For the POC, we'd like to run a 48-hour benchmark with synthetic traffic matching our triage load, and we'll want root-cause traces. Can Redwood provide tracing hooks and token-level latency breakdown?
04:17 Ravi Menon: Yes — Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks. We'll include a benchmark plan and the load script — I'll own that.
04:30 Maya Flores: Are there any hard stops on contract length? We usually prefer 12 month with option to extend, but want flexible exit if quality regressions occur.
04:40 Jamie Ortega: Standard terms allow 12 month contracts; we also offer canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies as part of the Optimize and Console tooling to minimize quality regressions. We can discuss an SLA credit structure for quality regressions in the SLA addendum.
04:55 Oliver Grant: On encryption — at-rest and in-transit are required. Will we get field-level encryption options and ability to push logs to our SIEM?
05:06 Ravi Menon: Yes, GCM TLS for in-transit and AES-256 at rest. For Private/Dedicated you can use your own KMS/HSM. Logs can be pushed to customer-managed destinations and we support integration to SIEMs via secure syslog or cloud logging exports.
05:20 Dr. Neha Singh: One of our concerns is vendor lock-in. If we later need to move models on-prem, how portable are the configs and prompts?
05:30 Jamie Ortega: We design config abstractions so you can pin model versions and export some artifacts; however runtime behavior does depend on the model and infra. We can do an export checklist as part of onboarding to minimize lock-in risk.
05:42 Evan Park: Back to SLAs — if we run the POC and see latency variance, what's remediation process? Auto fallback?
05:49 Ravi Menon: We have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants and capacity tiers; for Dedicated there are autoscaling/burst options. If latency exceeds the SLA, we trigger incident response, a root-cause analysis and then SLA credits according to the addendum.
06:05 Maya Flores: Legal also wants to see indemnity/limitation language specifically for third-party data processors and subprocessor lists. How are subprocessors disclosed?
06:15 Jamie Ortega: We publish a subprocessor list and maintain a change notification process. For MSA we can include the list as an exhibit and agree to notice before adding new subprocessors.
06:26 Oliver Grant: Do you support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning? We need SSO for our internal users to access the console.
06:34 Ravi Menon: Yes SAML 2.0 and SCIM are supported; we can set up a test tenant to validate provisioning flows. We'll demo that in the onboarding runbook.
06:45 Dr. Neha Singh: One other item — can Redwood sign a data processing addendum that includes subprocessor obligations and standard EU SCCs? We're partially subject to GDPR for EU patients.
06:58 Jamie Ortega: We include DPA language and can add SCCs where required. For EU residency we can pin region and also offer Private deployment if needed.
07:08 Maya Flores: On pricing approvals, can you provide a simple TCO estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted for our expected 10M tokens/month? Procurement prefers clear monthly commit numbers.
07:20 Jamie Ortega: We'll send a detailed sheet, but high-level: Dedicated lowers per-token unit cost via reserved capacity — we'll put two scenarios in the pricing sheet: hosted with burst and dedicated reserved with a monthly commit.
07:31 Maya Flores: That'd be great. Also our finance team needs invoice timing and PO-to-invoice SLAs.
07:36 Jamie Ortega: Invoices are monthly for hosted; for Dedicated we can do monthly or quarterly invoices per the contract. We'll note payment terms in the MSA redline.
07:46 Evan Park: For the benchmark, we want to include a mix of short chat queries and longer summaries to test KV cache behavior. We'll share a sample corpus.
07:55 Ravi Menon: Perfect. Send the profile and we'll tune batching and quantization recommendations; Optimize can suggest profiles based on the workload.
08:03 Oliver Grant: Any known compliance gaps we should be aware of? For example, are there any unsupported certifications or controls relevant to healthcare?
08:12 Jamie Ortega: We support SOC2, ISO where applicable; HIPAA support is available via Business Associate Agreements for certain plans — we'll flag that in the DPA and legal exhibit.
08:22 Maya Flores: If we sign a BAA, we'll need the security questionnaire answered fully. Can you fill ours?
08:27 Jamie Ortega: Yes, we'll complete the security questionnaire. We'll also attach SOC2 as backup.
08:33 Dr. Neha Singh: Quick note — in the MSA we want a clear exit assistance clause to ensure we can export logs and models if needed.
08:40 Jamie Ortega: Noted. We can include an exit assistance addendum with exports and data retention windows.
08:46 Maya Flores: Last part — timeline recap?
08:49 Jamie Ortega: Sure. Action items recap: Redwood to send redlined MSA and DPA with SCCs where needed; Security will share SOC2 and pen-test link; Ravi will prepare the benchmark plan; Maya to confirm procurement sign-off date.
09:05 Oliver Grant: Sounds good. If we can get those docs within a week, legal will review and push to final approval.
09:12 Jamie Ortega: Great — we'll aim to get the MSA redline and security docs out within 48–72 hours.
09:18 Maya Flores: Thanks everyone. We'll expect the MSA and security links and will follow up by email with our internal counsel comments.
09:25 Jamie Ortega: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the deck and security links.
09:30 End of recording.

Notes and references shared: Redwood onboarding deck (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/onboarding), Security docs (placeholder link), Pricing sheet to be attached in follow-up.

Transcript quirks: occasional mis-labels (speaker 2/3), minor transcription errors ("sock two" for SOC2), and some run-on phrases as typical for voice transcripts.
